newsitem.title: NIGERIA: African producers of gum arabic to sanitise trade.
newsitem.headline: African producers of gum arabic to sanitise trade.

text.p: Producers of gum arabic, a vital industry raw material produced only in Africa's savannah belt, plan to meet in Lagos this month to find ways to sanitise the export trade in the commodity, the organisers said on Wednesday.

They told a news conference in Lagos that the seven gum arabic producing nations would form an association at the end of the conference on November 29 but denied it would be a cartel like the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).
"An Association of African Producers of Gum Arabic and its Nigerian chapter are expected to emerge at the end of the event," said Chidume Okoro, chairman of Tadacon Nigeria Limited.
The company is a major exporter of the commodity from Nigeria and is organising the conference with the Nigerian Export Promotion Council and the Nigerian Import Export Bank.
"Our intention is to sanitise the market. We aim to improve quality by setting standards and influencing price," he added.
The seven nations are Sudan, the biggest producer, Nigeria, Niger, Chad, Senegal, Mali and Mauritania. Their trade ministers are expected to attend the closed-door meeting in Lagos.
Together they produce the estimated annual world output of 50,000 metric tonnes, almost all of which is shipped to developed countries for processing into industrial raw material.

The commodity, otherwise known as Acasia Senegalese after Senegal where it has its origin, is widely used in the food, soft drinks, pharmaceuticals, confectionery, textile, printing and cosmetics industries.
Most industries use it as a stabilising agent. Drugs manufactuers use it to coat tablets and brewers and food firms use it as a preservative.

Nigeria is the second biggest producer with annual output of 5,000 metric tonnes and income of one billion naira ($12.5 million). But Okoro said because of adulteration the Nigerian crop was discounted by about 30 percent in the international market.
The conference will be preceeded by a two-day seminar on export marketing and quality control.
Okoro said Indian and Lebanese exporters, who were very active in the gum arabic trade, were supporting the conference.
He said worldwide there were seven major buyers of gum arabic including the Marubeni and Toyota groups in Japan and others in the United States, Britain, Germany and France.
"They are a cartel. They don't produce gum arabic but they set the price," he said.
The price of the commodity has plunged to $2,200 per tonne currently from $6,500 in 1992.

Okoro said: "The outrageous thing is that this is a 100 percent African commodity not produced anywhere else and what happens is that they buy it for $2,200 per tonne, process it and ship the processed gum arabic back to us at $14,000 per tonne."
